newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Jan C/A, trade balance improves - cen.bank.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Jan C/A, trade balance improves - cen.bank.

text.p: The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) said on Friday that the position of the current account and the trade balance in January was better than expected and represented an improvement on January figures for recent years.
"The January (preliminary) figures are certainly better than the past few years' current account and foreign trade figures," NBH President Gyorgy Suranyi told a news conference.
He added that according to the NBH's figures, exports and imports have increased this year, and the rise in imports did not speed up relative to exports.

Suranyi did not disclose numbers, saying the January and February balance of payments figures would be published later than usual due to technical changes the NBH was implementing in its calculations methods.

The current account deficit was $294 million in January 1996, while the trade gap calculated in cash flow terms was $302 million. In December current account deficit was $501 million and the trade gap was $417 million.

Suranyi added that he did not expect the planned abolition of the current 4 percent import surcharge to increase imports by more than a few tens of millions of dollars and said it was unlikely to affect the current account significantly.
Hungary first introduced an eight percent import surcharge in March 1995 as part of its austerity programme which succeeded in reining in the soaring current account and trade deficits.
The surcharge, currently four percent, is to be phased out completely by July 1.
Hungary's current account deficit target for 1997 is $1.5 to $2.0 billion, compared with a figure of $1.68 billion for 1996.
